glosses: To create a rattling sound by shaking or striking.

examples.text: to rattle a chain
Rattle the can of cat treats if you need to find Fluffy.
It was a deflating end to the drama for the hosts and they appeared ruffled, with Bolton going close to a leveller when Johan Elmander rattled the bar with a header from Matt Taylor’s cross.

glosses: To scare, startle, unsettle, or unnerve.

examples.text: “Tut!” said old Bittlesham. “Tut is right”, I agreed. Then the rumminess of the thing struck me. “But if you haven’t dropped a parcel over the race,” I said, “why are you looking so rattled?”

That United were rattled, mentally as well as at times physically – legitimately so – was beyond question. Nick Powell clipped a crisp drive a foot over the bar, but otherwise Milton Keynes had the best of the remainder of the first half.
The German authorities are still trying to determine what damage their mole may have done. But the discovery of a double agent has rattled German political circles.

glosses: To make a rattling noise; to make noise by or from shaking.

examples.text: I wish the dashboard in my car would quit rattling.

glosses: To assail, annoy, or stun with a rattling noise.

examples.text: Sound but another [drum], and another shall / As loud as thine rattle the welkin’s ear.

glosses: To scold; to rail at.

examples.text: This came to the Bishop's Ear, who presently sent for the Curate, Rattled him to some Tune, with Menaces to the Highest Degree

glosses: To drive or ride briskly, so as to make a clattering.

examples.text: We rattled along for a couple of miles.

glosses: To make a clatter with one's voice; to talk rapidly and idly; often with on or away.

examples.text: She rattled on for an hour.

glosses: To experience withdrawal from drugs.
Object that rattles.
Any of various plants of the genera Rhinanthus and Pedicularis, whose seeds produce a rattling noise in the wind.
Object that rattles.
A baby’s toy designed to make sound when shaken, usually containing loose grains or pellets in a hollow container.

examples.text: Pleas'd with a rattle, tickled with a straw.

glosses: Object that rattles.
A musical instrument that makes a rattling sound.

examples.text: The rattles of Isis and the cymbals of Brasilea nearly enough resemble each other.

glosses: Object that rattles.
A device which produces a loud rattling sound, especially one having a ratchet mechanism and spun round on a handle.

examples.text: [T]he footpath to Hendon went across hay and corn fields and in summer the sound of rattles used by boys hired to "fray" the birds from the crops was familiar.

glosses: Object that rattles.
The set of rings at the end of a rattlesnake's tail which produce a rattling sound.

examples.text: The rattle of the rattlesnake is composed of the hardened terminal scales, loosened in succession, but not cast off, and modified in form so as to make a series of loose, hollow joints.

2017, Kenny Salwey, J. Scott Bestul, The Last River Rat: Kenny Salwey's Life in the Wild
The majority of snakes were killed on the spot, as a snaker only had to produce the rattles to collect the bounty.

glosses: Rattling sound.
A rapid succession of percussive sounds, as made by loose objects shaking or vibrating against one another.

examples.text: I wish they would fix the rattle under my dashboard.
The rattle of a drum.

For a few minutes, the sharp cracking of guns ahead warned them to haste, but finally the reports dwindled to an occasional shot, presently ceasing altogether. Nor was this less ominous than the rattle of musketry, for it suggested but a single solution to the little band of rescuers—that the illy garrisoned village had already succumbed to the onslaught of a superior force.

glosses: Rattling sound.
Noisy, rapid talk; babble.

examples.text: All this adoe about the golden age is but an empty rattle and frivolous conceipt.

glosses: Rattling sound.
Trivial chatter; gossip.

examples.text: “And pray where, Lady Honoria,” cried Mrs. Delvile, “do you contrive to pick up all this rattle?”

glosses: Rattling sound.
A noisy, senseless talker; a jabberer.

examples.text: ‘Sir James is a young Man of an amiable disposition, and excellent character;—a little too much of the Rattle perhaps, but a year or two will rectify that […].’
It may seem strange that a man who wrote with so much perspicuity, vivacity, and grace, should have been, whenever he took a part in conversation, an empty, noisy, blundering rattle.

glosses: Rattling sound.
A scolding; a sharp rebuke.
Rattling sound.
A rough noise produced in the throat by air passing through obstructed airways; croup; a death rattle.
Alternative form of rottol: a former Middle Eastern and North African unit of dry weight usually equal to 1–5 lb (0.5–2.5 kg).

glosses: Moulinet de bois qui fait un bruit aigre utilisé dans divers rituels (le viatique, etc.) et par les lépreux pour avertir de leur passage.

examples.text: Sonner la crécelle.

Oh ! le viatique ! comme on était fier quand on pouvait l’accompagner !… Sous un petit dais de velours rouge, marchait le prêtre, portant l’hostie et les saintes huiles. Deux enfants de chœur soutenaient le dais, deux autres l’escortaient avec de gros falots dorés. Un cinquième marchait devant, en agitant une crécelle.

Il y a des claquoirs simples ou doubles, que l’on appelle : claquoirs, battoirs, crécelles ou cricri, routelles, tartarelles ou tourterelles, dont la forme la plus connue est celle de Corbie, qui ressemble à un tonnelet de fer.

Un étrange bruit de crécelles s’élève du fond de Saxon, suivi aussitôt d’un concert de voix enfantines qui chantent sur un ton traînard : « Voilà… voilà…, pour le premier. » Et puis encore le bruit des crécelles… (…) c’est la tournée traditionnelle des enfants qui remplacent les cloches envolées pour Rome durant la semaine sainte ; ils vont de maison en maison annoncer que l’heure de l’office est venue.
Le bruit de la vérité les épouvante comme la crécelle d’un lépreux.
Avant d’arriver à la lisière nous sortîmes tous de nos gibecières les grosses crécelles de bois avec lesquelles, pendant le temps de Pâques, on remplace les cloches.

– Bon, tu as raison… mais pour ce qui est des clochettes, des sonnettes, ça non, je les entends… et aussi des bruits de crécelle, le crépitement des fleurs de celluloïd rouges, roses, mauves, tournant au vent…

glosses: Élytre d’un insecte, dont le frottement produit un bruit évoquant celui d’une crécelle.

examples.text: Des milliers de grillons ont pris possession de ces grands bâtiments déserts, on ne sait où poser le pied pour n’en pas écraser ; ils font tant de bruit avec leurs petites crécelles, que l’on a de la peine à s’entendre parler. Malgré l’amour que je professe pour les grillons, amour que j’ai exprimé en prose et en vers, je dois convenir qu’il y en avait un peu trop.

glosses: Personne qui a une voix de crécelle.

examples.text: Mlle Maria, soixante-dix ans, n’a plus qu’une voix de crécelle que M. l’Archiprêtre fait taire d’un geste impératif : – « Ah ! s’il m’avait, dit-elle pour toute vengeance, entendue à vingt ans, quand j’étais le rossignol de la paroisse ? »
Je l’ai entendu, maître Mouche ; il a une voix de crécelle et il parle en termes choisis, mais j’eusse préféré qu’il ne choisît pas du tout ses termes.
Ouh ! là, je la reconnais cette crécelle furibarde.

L’eau fraîche y bruissait sur de petits cailloux polis ; on y entendait de très loin, et perdus en murmure confus, les bruits du grand bassin, les rires des jeunes femmes et la voix de crécelle de Tétouara……
